author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected under the same rules as booking; the correction changes that visit in place rather than adding another, and returns to the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened at GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, then the existing visit form (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm, model attribute visit) shows that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when a new description and a date later than today are POSTed to the same address, then that visit is updated and the response redirects to the owner detail page
given a booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet has the same number of visits as before (no additional visit record)
given a booked visit, when a correction with a blank description or a date of today or earlier is submitted, then the visit is unchanged and the form is redisplayed
edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet not belonging to the named owner, is refused
edge case 4: a request to correct a visit that does not exist is refused rather than showing an empty form
non_goals: cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-4, narrowed NG-5)
an edit link or any visible entry point on the owner detail page (owner deferred to a follow-up request)
correcting a visit to a date of today or earlier, including keeping a past visit's date (open question in docs/prd.md)
changing which pet a visit belongs to

Narrowest readings taken without owner input: the rule for refusing a mismatched or missing visit follows REQ-VIS-001 edge case 1 and REQ-OWN-003 edge case 2; validation is identical to booking per the intake. The REQ-VIS-002 earlier-visits list on the reused form carries no new requirement for the correction view.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Existing pattern with small adjustments. The correction runs through the Owner aggregate exactly as booking does (system-design.md § Contracts invariants paragraph: Pet and Visit persisted only by cascade from Owner; OwnerRepository is the sole write path). Owner -> Pet -> Visit resolution by identity, the persisted Visit is changed in place, then owners.save(owner). Adjustments: (1) Pet gains a lookup of one persisted visit by identity, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) (Owner.java:126), so aggregate traversal lives in the model, not the controller; (2) VisitController's class-wide @ModelAttribute("visit") (VisitController.java:63-81) currently constructs and attaches a new Visit to the pet on every request - it must attach a new visit only on the booking routes, otherwise the correction save cascades an extra visit and breaks the 'same number of visits' criterion; (3) the non-future-date check (VisitController.java:99-101) becomes one check shared by booking and correction - this is the rule the recorded controller-rule deviation names (architecture-principles.md line 91, system-design.md § Package Structure), so reuse is covered; a copy or any new rule in the controller is not. Basis: grep and file reads (IDE oracle not connected). Docs written: Contracts rows (Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, VisitController) carry REQ-VIS-003; invariants paragraph records in-place correction; new § Scale and Load row; Known Defects row for the booking route's owner binding; ADR index row for the narrowing ADR.
integration_points: Entry point GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit binds onto the persisted Visit resolved from the owner graph, behind an allow-list of date and description (security-principles.md § Mass assignment row; id stays disallowed). The Owner must not be request-bound on the correction POST: take it from the model without binding. A binder narrowing that also applies to the booking route is acceptable, since booking offers only those fields, but it changes binding on a route the slice's bullets do not name - say so in the build record.

Repository boundary (OwnerRepository): the existing @MockitoBean in VisitControllerTests is the conscious exception - OwnerRepository is a Spring Data JpaRepository whose inherited surface makes a hand-written double unworkable inside a @WebMvcTest slice (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy). Seed a real Owner/Pet/Visit graph; assert on graph state (visit count, the visit's date and description) and on save()/no save(), not on stub interactions alone.
Framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).

Template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html has no th:action, so the form posts back to the edit address; the heading already drops 'New' for a persisted visit. The button label key addVisit may stay; any new label needs a key in every locale bundle (REQ-LANG-002).

patterns.description: lookup-by-identity skipping unsaved entries; model the Pet visit lookup on it
refusal of a missing owner or mismatched pet; a missing or mismatched visit is refused the same way (PRD edge cases 3-4 follow REQ-VIS-001 edge case 1)
existing init/process edit pair under an owner; route shape for the correction handlers

risks.risk: Class-wide visit model attribute attaches a new Visit on the correction routes; cascade then persists an extra visit (Contracts invariants: cascade from Owner).
risks.mitigation: Scope new-visit construction to the booking routes; the correction resolves the existing visit. theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddAVisitToThePet guards it.

risks.risk: Mass assignment on the correction POST: binding onto a persisted Visit and a request-bound Owner (security-principles.md § Mass assignment; system-design.md § Known Defects booking-owner row).
risks.mitigation: Allow-list date and description; Owner not request-bound on the correction route.

risks.risk: Validation failure must leave the visit unchanged; binding mutates the loaded entity before validation.
risks.mitigation: No save on errors; open-in-view is off (system-design.md § Persistence), so the in-memory mutation is discarded with the request.

risks.risk: Correction path scales with pets per owner and visits per pet (system-design.md § Scale and Load, visit booking and correction row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: in-memory scan of the loaded collections.

risks.risk: Business-rule drift: duplicating the non-future-date check or adding a new rule in the controller is a fresh catalog violation (architecture-principles.md Web controller row, line 91).
risks.mitigation: One shared check for both flows; no new controller rule.

risks.risk: Hard-coded flash message: existing flash strings are hard-coded English, and a new one widens that gap (REQ-LANG-002).
risks.mitigation: Add no new hard-coded flash string; the criteria require only the redirect.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. ADR index: added the row for docs/adr/2026-10-25-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md and annotated the 2026-08-08 row's status, at the product expert's request. The narrowing ADR, the 2026-08-08 status line, and docs/prd.md were written by product-requirements-expert (prd-entry line 3 notes), not this dispatch. Open questions recorded rather than waited on: (a) the Known Defects row for the booking route binding owner fields is derived from code and unconfirmed, and is outside this slice's scope; (b) docs/system-design.md had no § Scale and Load section, so this dispatch created it with one row; (c) past-visit date retention stays the PRD open question and a slice non-goal. author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Mass assignment: the new correction POST binds only the visit's date and description. VisitController.java:56-58 reads `@InitBinder("visit")` / `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description")`, and the class-wide binder at VisitController.java:51-53 (`dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")`) still applies to every binder. The owner on the edit route is `@ModelAttribute(binding = false) Owner owner`, so no request parameter reaches the saved owner graph. The visit allow-list also narrows the existing booking path; it does not weaken it. The booking path's pre-existing owner binding is recorded as a Known Defect in docs/system-design.md, and this change does not extend it to the new route.

Cross-entity tampering (IDOR within the demo's no-auth baseline): every request re-resolves owner -> pet -> visit from the path. Pet.getVisit only searches that pet's own persisted visits (`if (!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id))`). A visitId belonging to another pet, or a petId the owner does not own, throws before any save; VisitControllerTests covers both cases plus an unknown visit, with `verify(this.owners, never()).save(any())`. This meets the security-principles.md row on trusting cross-request state.

Validation on the persisting path: processUpdateVisitForm takes `@Valid Visit visit` (Visit.description is `@NotBlank`). The non-future-date check was extracted into rejectNonFutureDate and is called on both booking and correction, so no existing check was removed.

Error output: the new IllegalArgumentException message carries only the two integer path variables (`"Visit with id " + visitId + " not found for pet with id " + petId`). No secret or user-supplied text can reach the error page that renders it.

XSS: the shared template createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders the visit and its previous visits only through th:text, which escapes by default, and its form has no th:action, so the correction posts back to its own edit URL. No unescaped output and no template-expression preprocessing were added.

Secret sweep: grepping added diff lines for password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|credential (case-insensitive) found nothing. Detection patterns for shell execution, file I/O, and Jackson typing do not apply: the only production changes are Pet.java and VisitController.java, which were read in full in the diff.

Supply chain: build.gradle is unchanged (`git diff --stat -- build.gradle` is empty). OWASP dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured in build.gradle, so no NVD match ran. Resolved runtime versions from `./gradlew dependencies`: Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, jackson-databind (tools.jackson) 3.1.5.

Surface widening: the two new GET and POST routes under /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit are stated in docs/system-design.md. They add no management exposure and no new privilege beyond the demonstration baseline.
